_comment: E16 against the roadmap's nine-item Definition of Done. Regenerate: tools/phase4_e16_dod_scorecard.py
standard: Game Solving Roadmap - From Reconstruction to Reliable Modding.md, 'Definition of Done for a solved subsystem' (9 items), plus the Phase-4 exit gate's 'without being explicitly bounded'.
why_not_the_promotion_tool: tools/phase4_promotion_preflight.py encodes these same nine dimensions 1:1 in the same order, but wraps them in campaign-registry, debt-ledger and packet scaffolding the written standard never requires. The standard is judged by review; the tool is one attempt to automate that judgement.
row_scope: the whole E16 row (scene flow, overlays, streaming, residency, unload, failure paths)
scope_caveat: Almost all E16 evidence covers ONE sub-area -- the three registered-chunk pointer tables. A row-level 'met' would be an overclaim, so each item states its own scope and `met_in_scope` is counted separately from `met`.

items.requirement: original behavior has a deterministic cold-boot reproduction with scene/media identity and observable assertions
items.established: movies/Phase4/Interpreter/E02_FreshLoad_Clover.movie.json is from_boot (5,562 frames) and drives boot -> frontend -> Clover Forest. Observable assertions exist and are automated: table occupancy must reach >= 30 slots and a loader clear or bulk zero must fire as a positive control.
items.missing: No cold-boot oracle for the overlay load path (MEMORY.BIN, FMV.BIN, LEVEL*.BIN), for unload, or for any failure/retry path. The 16 campaign movies are state-anchored, not cold-boot.
items.next_experiment: Record one from-boot movie that enters and LEAVES a level, so unload has an oracle; assert overlay region A contents at both boundaries.

items.requirement: relevant callers, callees, callbacks, indirect tables, overlays, readers, writers, and downstream consumers have been enumerated
items.established: Readers/writers enumerated and CLOSED by materialisation: only 5 sites in the entire text segment can form a pointer into these windows and all 5 are already enumerated, so no deliberate access exists outside the known set. Incidental readers enumerated as a family (22 hoisted-load sites). Overlay scope censused at true load bases. 30 bounded_residuals, 0 rejections.
items.missing: Row-wide the frontier is NOT enumerated: the streaming table 0x8007EFE8, overlay region A and its 42 entries, the high heap allocator, and the LEVEL.RAW/DAT/BIN asset families are unmeasured. Item 2 is met for the tables, not for E16.
items.next_experiment: Run the materialisation census against 0x8007EFE8 and the region-A base; if either yields sites outside a known set, that is the next frontier to close.

items.requirement: important fields have widths, signedness, ownership, valid domains, initialization, reset rules, and confidence-backed evidence
items.established: Each table is a u32 pointer array indexed marker*4; occupied windows and slot addressing are pinned in Canon; the marker domain is fully mapped from the loader's own dispatch; initialization (loader clears at 0x8003A3B8/BC) and the per-load reset rule are code-confirmed.
items.missing: Ownership is documented informally rather than as a typed-state record, and nothing is typed for region A, the streaming table, or the high heap. The player block's extent -- which decides whether the 0x58..0x5F window is merely ADJACENT to it -- has never been formally bounded.
items.next_experiment: Bound the player state block's extent, then record widths/ownership/reset for the streaming table 0x8007EFE8.

items.requirement: behavior is characterized through creation, repeated use, retirement, death/respawn, pause, scene transition, and reload
items.established: Creation and one transition are measured: two tables are cleared per load and one is never cleared, leaving 36 pointers dangling into reused high heap with 36/36 markers overwritten -- a hazard the retail game never trips because nothing reads them after.
items.missing: Death/respawn, pause, level EXIT/unload, scene-to-scene reload and repeated re-entry are all uncharacterised. The measured scope is a single transition in a single direction.
items.next_experiment: Replay a movie that enters a level, dies, respawns and exits; sample the three tables at each boundary.

items.requirement: call/return, live state, stack/ra, hi/lo, GTE, delay-slot, memory-effect, callback, overlay and asset-loading contracts are known at every boundary the subsystem crosses
items.scope: overlay entry ABI and the loader's own contract
items.established: Overlay ABI characterised and bracketed by two opposite-erring detectors to 42/42 entry points; the loader's dispatch, header layout and class split are code-confirmed from its own instructions rather than inferred.
items.missing: 18 of the 42 entries are confirmed by only ONE of the two detectors, and no runtime check has been made that a scene actually CALLS the entries its overlay implements. Asset-loading contracts at failure boundaries are untouched.
items.next_experiment: execTrace a range watch over region A during a level load and record which of the 42 entries actually execute.

items.requirement: every applicable level, objective, enemy/actor variant, special mode, and exceptional path is covered
items.scope: all 16 campaign levels, for the three tables
items.established: 16/16 campaign levels validated at 60 Hz plus the reference movie (17/17 usable, 1,930 events), every event from an enumerated or characterised PC. NOT FALSIFIED.
items.missing: Exceptional paths -- load failure, retry, disc error, unload -- are uncovered. Breadth is across LEVELS, not across the row's modes: FMV and MEMORY overlays are not exercised by these movies.
items.next_experiment: Cover the FMV and MEMORY overlay load paths, then an induced load failure if one can be provoked safely.

items.requirement: interactions with player state, physics, rendering, animation, audio, HUD, objectives, save/load and scene transitions are validated
items.established: The rendering interaction is characterised end to end: registered chunks are frontend VRAM images uploaded on demand by level_texture_stage / vram_upload_wait, 46/46 satisfying their consumer-derived size law and visually confirmed by decoding. The player-state relationship is bounded as ADJACENCY, not overlap.
items.missing: No validation against physics, animation, audio, HUD, objectives or save/load. Scene transitions are touched only by the single lifecycle sample. This is the least-served item and is honestly OPEN.
items.next_experiment: Pick the two interactions most likely to bite -- save/load (does any registered pointer reach the save schema?) and scene transition -- and validate those first.

items.requirement: matching or reviewed semantic source represents the complete behavior, and remaining byte/layout mismatches are explicitly bounded
items.scope: the loader and the two consumers
items.established: The loader exists as hand-written asm that assembles against pristine, and both consumers are decompiled and reviewed in Canon with their addresses pinned.
items.missing: No C for the loader -- hand asm is matching, not semantic source -- and no enumeration of remaining byte/layout mismatches as bounded. Nothing for region A or the streaming path.
items.next_experiment: Decompile 0x8003A318 to reviewable C via the existing dc_m2c_seed pipeline and diff behavior against the hand asm.

items.requirement: Canon describes confirmed original behavior, Experiments hold reproductions and causal evidence, and Mods describe private state and intended changes
items.scope: the whole E16 row (scene flow, overlays, streaming, residency, unload, failure paths)
items.established: Canon: one system note, three memory notes, two function notes, all carrying the completeness argument and the incidental-reader warning. Experiments: four, each with its reproduction and its retractions recorded. The roadmap carries the row's history including corrections.
items.missing: No Mods note -- correctly, since no E16 mod exists. That clause binds only where private state or an intended change exists.
items.next_experiment: None required; refresh if an overlay/streaming mod is authored.

verdict: E16 is NOT solved by the Definition of Done. 2 of 9 items met (1 met row-wide, 1 met within a declared sub-area), 6 partial, 1 open. The strongest item is 2, complete frontier, which is CLOSED for the three pointer tables by an argument that does not depend on runtime silence. The weakest is 7, cross-system behavior, which is honestly open. Item 2 being met is exactly what the roadmap asks -- 'enumerated', with the remainder explicitly bounded -- and not the empty-intersection-set bar quoted in the B06 note.
